activity.notes: Frumentius became the first bishop associated with Aksum and helped establish Christianity in the kingdom. The consecration is traditionally dated around 326 (some modern summaries give a slightly later range), while older biographical references place his death around 360. ATLAS therefore records a deliberately approximate 326–360 religious-activity interval rather than false exact episcopal boundaries.

sources.title: Frumentius — Encyclopaedia Britannica, 11th ed. (Wikisource)
sources.citation_text: The reference identifies Frumentius as founder of the Abyssinian church, says he gained influence at Axum, and dates his episcopal consecration to 326 and his life approximately to c.300-c.360.

sources.title: Aksum — Britannica
sources.citation_text: Britannica describes Aksum as the major northeastern African kingdom of the early Christian era and notes the Christianization of its kings in the fourth century.
